title: Semantic icon roles
note: The canonical 20 semantic icon roles. Components ask for a ROLE; the theme's iconRoles map (themes/theme-*.json) and the set files (icons/sets/*.json) decide which glyph answers. This is the list a theme must map in full — a role with no consumer today is still required, because the contract is the role list, not the current registry. 'consumers' is derived from the iconRole declarations in contract/anatomy/*.json and is verified by scripts/check-icons.py; an empty list means no registry anatomy claims the role yet.

close.meaning: Dismiss the container you are inside — a dialog, sheet, toast or alert — and return focus to whatever opened it. Always an interactive control with an accessible name; never decorative.

dismiss.meaning: Remove one item from a set without closing anything around it: a chip or tag delete, a removable filter, a per-row clear. Every mapped set draws it with the same glyph as close; the roles stay separate because they carry different labels and a theme may swap one without the other.

expand.meaning: Reveal content that is currently hidden below the trigger, and mark the direction it will open. Themes usually rotate this glyph on open rather than swapping it for collapse.

collapse.meaning: The inverse of expand: fold content, a rail or a panel away. Distinct from close because nothing is dismissed — the content stays mounted and addressable.

back.meaning: Step to the previous item in an ordered sequence: previous month, previous slide, previous page. The direction is logical, not physical, so it mirrors under RTL.

forward.meaning: Step to the next item in an ordered sequence. Also serves as the breadcrumb separator, where it is a static direction marker between links rather than a control.

search.meaning: Marks a field or command surface as a query input. Presentational — the field's own label carries the meaning, so this glyph is aria-hidden.

add.meaning: Create a new item, or increment a value. No registry anatomy declares it yet: it belongs to app-level toolbars and stepper fields rather than to any primitive. Themes must still map it, because the role list is the contract, not the current consumer set.

remove.meaning: Subtract, decrement or delete a row. Doubles as the neutral dash where a separator glyph is needed, which is why input-otp uses it between groups.

overflow.meaning: 'There is more here' — the collapsed remainder of a set: hidden breadcrumbs, elided page numbers, an actions menu behind a single trigger.

error.meaning: Something failed or a value is invalid. Carries the status-critical tone and always accompanies text — the glyph is never the only signal that something is wrong.

warning.meaning: Proceed with care: a destructive confirmation, or a condition that has not failed yet. Carries the status-warning tone.

success.meaning: Confirmed, checked, selected. The same glyph does duty as the check mark in checkbox, in a selected select option and in a pressed toggle, because all three mean 'yes, this is on'.

info.meaning: A neutral notice. The default status glyph for alerts and toasts before any tone is chosen.

calendar.meaning: Date entry — the trigger that opens a date picker. No registry anatomy declares it: the calendar anatomy IS the picker surface, so the trigger lives on the composing field rather than inside the calendar.

user.meaning: A person: avatar fallback when no image resolves, account menu, assignee.

upload.meaning: Send a file from the device. No registry anatomy declares it yet (there is no file-input primitive), but themes must map it so app-level dropzones resolve.

external.meaning: The destination leaves the current context — a new tab, another product. The fact must also appear in the link's accessible name; the glyph alone does not announce it. Not yet declared by any registry anatomy.

drag.meaning: A grab handle: this element can be moved or resized by pointer. Always paired with a keyboard equivalent, because a handle alone is not an accessible affordance.

loading.meaning: Work is in progress and its duration is unknown. The only role with required motion — a continuous rotation that must degrade to a static indicator under prefers-reduced-motion.
